message: In the under-deck Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) retrofit (C1), the detuned comfort and stroke at plus-or-minus 5 percent frequency drift has uncertain margin, Manager. To check it I used two-degree-of-freedom steady-state simulation (the detuned damping estimate (E8)) building on the optimal Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) sizing (E4) and the controlled-response stroke estimate (E6). I found effective damping of 0.064 dimensionless even at plus 5 percent detune with deck acceleration below 0.5 metres per second squared and stroke below 12 millimetres within 30 millimetre clearance, according to Den Hartog, 1934 and Human Induced Vibrations of Steel Structures (HIVOSS), 2008. I propose retaining 400 kilograms at 1.86 Hertz (Hz) with 0.086 Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) damping ratio plus slotted spring seats for re-tuning. My position: not ready because support fatigue needs closure. In the concealed under-deck support interface (C2), the bolted cross-frame connection force for the 400 kilogram added mass has no agreed sizing load, Retrofit Integration Architect and Structural Dynamics Lead. To check it I used static weight calculation (the static weight calculation (E9)) combined with spring stiffness from the optimal Tuned Mass Damper (TMD) sizing (E4) times stroke from the controlled-response stroke estimate (E6). I found 3924 Newtons static plus about 500 Newtons dynamic for about 4424 Newtons peak per 400 kilogram unit, according to Den Hartog, 1934. I propose sizing four M16 bolts per unit to that peak with fatigue detail per Eurocode. My position: not ready because you must confirm fatigue before comfort sign-off.
